We see a lot of customers who'd benefit from Redwood's Dedicated and Private modes alongside our integration services.

Hi Aria — great to meet you.

Love the concept and think a 4-week accelerator makes a lot of sense for joint GTM and rapid proof-of-value. I put together a concise Partner Accelerator checklist below and attached it as a PDF so you can share with your delivery leads. This covers the minimum inputs we need from your side and items Redwood will own.

High-level checklist (summary):
- Week 0 (prep): account intake, network & VPC requirements, data access approval, model selection guidance
- Week 1 (sandbox): environment provisioning, test dataset sync, basic integration (API calls + auth)
- Week 2 (integration): prefix caching, prompt engineering handoff, KV cache sizing, observability hooks
- Week 3 (hardening): latency tuning, autoscaling policy test, canary rollout plan, security review
- Week 4 (handoff): enablement workshop (2 hours), runbook, customer-facing playbook, handover to CS

Pre-reqs we typically request from partners: basic network topology, list of supported customer cloud regions, and a technical contact for firewall/KMS coordination.

I attached: partner-accelerator-checklist.pdf and a template for "Nexa technical requirements" (nexa-technical-requirements.xlsx) — feel free to fill the sheet and send back.

Next steps: can we lock a kickoff the week of Sep 13? If that works I will schedule an internal readiness sync (30m) with Marissa (enablement lead) and Sean (partner ops) to prepare the accelerator materials.

Thanks — looking forward to working together.

—
Kimberly Park
Director, Partner Programs | Redwood Inference

Kim / Aria — quick technical add from me.

A few items to highlight for Nexa's delivery team so the sandbox -> prod path is smooth:
- VPN vs VPC peering: we recommend VPC peering for Dedicated installs; VPN for early sandboxing only.
- Model variants: start with a curated open model from Redwood's catalog that matches the customer SLAs; we'll provide a performance profile so you can estimate token cost and latency.
- KV cache sizing: estimate based on expected session concurrency; we can run a quick load profile during Week 2.
- Observability: include the lightweight tracing hook we provide (one-line SDK instrument) in dev before Week 2 so we have token and latency baselines.

I'll prepare a short "technical readiness checklist" slide (10 min) we can present during the kickoff.

Marissa Cole
